The Journey
The Journey ↗
RF / SPATIAL MODEL

A place observes.
A world takes shape.

From non-optical public-space awareness to perception as infrastructure. The invention brings radio-frequency observations, physical constraints and shared spatial intelligence into one evolving system.

01 / The original question

Understand the situation.
Reduce the need for imagery.

The first question was rooted in public safety: could distributed RF infrastructure reconstruct a situation without making an optical image its primary representation?

Provisional specification / April 2026

SecureTower.

A variable-geometry MIMO array, local signal conditioning and an edge-to-cloud reconstruction pipeline. The proposed emergency-response embodiment activated nearby towers after an SOS trigger and fused their observations into a spatial scene.

Public-space awarenessRF-derived scene reconstructionEvent-triggered sensing
Complete specification / September 2026

A common perception layer.

The architecture expands into a persistent RF Spatial World Model. Its observations retain source and timing information; alternate interpretations remain open; uncertainty guides the next sensing operation. Independent applications consume the resulting spatial state.

Persistent world modelPhysics-informed inferenceAdaptive sensing
02 / The change in architecture

From a reconstructed scene
to a shared spatial state.

Observation, interpretation and action form a loop. Explore the relationships that turn separate measurements into information other systems can use.

Observations retain transmitter, receiver, acquisition time and spatial relationships. Different positions contribute complementary evidence.

03 / The research journey

An architecture developed
over time.

Physics, systems research and a path toward manufacturing shaped the transition from a public-safety concept into a broader perception infrastructure.

  1. 18+ months

    Physics before a product.

    Full-time research began with the sensing physics and system architecture. Roughly the first year included discussions with senior academics and researchers with telecom, aerospace and RF experience.

  2. 8 April 2026

    The provisional foundation.

    The provisional specification formalized variable-geometry MIMO sensing, distributed SecureTowers and RF-based reconstruction for situational awareness.

  3. September 2026

    Perception as infrastructure.

    The complete specification develops a persistent world-model architecture. The founder reports filing the specification and publication of the application in the Indian Patent Journal.

  4. In parallel

    A route toward hardware.

    Engagement with specialized RF hardware manufacturers in China and Taiwan explores the manufacturability and production requirements of custom RF, synchronization and distributed-compute infrastructure.

  5. Now / Proof of concept

    Make the reconstruction measurable.

    The core AI and physics inference architecture is being developed through training-data generation and model iteration. The next test is an end-to-end RF-observation-to-world-model demonstration.

04 / Inside the inference architecture

Every interpretation
answers to the evidence.

The complete specification treats reconstruction as an inverse problem. Learned models propose spatial states; physical models predict their RF responses; consistency checks update the alternatives.

01 / The measurement

A response shaped by the environment.

Yij(t)=Hij(t)Xi(t)+Cij(t)+Nij(t)

For transmitter i and receiver j, the known signal X is modified by the environment response H. Interference C and noise N are retained in the observation model.

Complete specification · pp. 20–21 ↗
02 / Proposal and prediction

Work in both directions.

Hk∼Finv(Y)Y^(a,Hk)=FEM(Hk,a)

The inverse model proposes candidate state Hₖ. The electromagnetic forward model predicts what an interrogation configuration a would observe if that candidate were correct.

Complete specification · pp. 40–41 ↗
03 / The consistency check

Compare prediction with observation.

Rk(a)=d(Yobs,Y^(a,Hk))

The discrepancy Rₖ informs whether a hypothesis is strengthened, weakened, retained or rejected. Cross-node geometry, temporal behavior and physical constraints also contribute to the update.

Complete specification · pp. 41–44 ↗
04 / The reconstruction objective

Several constraints. One reconstruction.

ℒ=λrℒRF+λgℒgeometry+λtℒtemporal+λpℒphysics+λsℒsemantic

RF agreement is evaluated alongside geometry, temporal continuity, physics and semantics. The weights λ depend on the reconstruction task.

Complete specification · p. 41 ↗
05 / The persistent representation

More than a 3D shape.

W(x,t)={G,M,O,K,C,U,P,H}

The world model keeps the supporting evidence and alternative hypotheses alongside the reconstructed spatial state.

Complete specification · pp. 46–47 ↗

06 / The adaptive loop

What remains uncertain
guides what comes next.

Uncertainty Uₜ informs the next sensing configuration Sₜ₊₁. A different node, transmitter–receiver pairing, spectral layer or waveform can provide the evidence needed to distinguish surviving hypotheses.

Complete specification · pp. 48–49 ↗
Wt→Ut→St+1→Rt+1→Wt+1World state → uncertainty → sensing → observations → updated state
05 / From architecture to evidence

Build the loop.
Measure the reconstruction.

The current proof-of-concept programme uses CARLA and NVIDIA Sionna to connect physical scenes, RF ray-tracing and model inference. LiDAR provides a reference against which reconstructed geometry can be evaluated.
